title: improv·artist · pixel (Manfred Mohr)
mutation_directive: improv artist: pixel via Manfred Mohr

v1.feedback: The hypercube geometry directly channels Mohr's cube-rotation studies and the 4D→3D perspective projection is faithful to his practice — the linked idea clearly drove the design. The restrained near-monochrome palette (warm white / cool steel / neutral) is appropriate, and the pixel-snap quantization is a nice nod to 'pixel' and Mohr's discrete digital aesthetic. Two improvements: the audio-reactive rotation, while engaging, means the form drifts into orientations where the tesseract reads as a flat tangle — consider clamping rotation rates or adding a slow auto-orbit fallback so the structure always reads in <2s even without mic input. Second, 20k particles on 32 edges is generous but the additive blending washes out edge distinction at vertices; try reducing point opacity or adding a faint line-segment pass so the wireframe skeleton stays legible beneath the particle cloud.

v2.feedback: The tesseract geometry is immediately legible — you see the hypercube wireframe within 2 seconds, and the 4D rotation planes (XW, YZ, XY) are a genuine nod to Mohr's cube-rotation studies rather than a cosmetic rename. The pixel-snap quantization in the vertex shader (floor to grid) is a smart touch that echoes Mohr's plotter-era discretization. Two things to push: the particle density per edge (280) produces a nearly solid wireframe that reads more 'glowing neon tube' than 'pointillist digital grid' — drop to ~80-120 particles with slightly larger point sizes to let the discrete pixel identity breathe. Second, the mic-reactive jitter is generic energy mapping with no Mohr-specific structure — consider driving the 4D rotation angles directly from audio bands so the projection itself morphs with sound, which would tie the interaction to the geometric concept rather than just wobbling particles.
